description:
compiler2 fails to decode a list literal whose LAST element is a function call.

Minimal repro:
  fn main(), do: dbg([Enum.reverse([1,2,3])])              -> ERROR
  fn main(), do: dbg([1, Enum.reverse([1,2,3])])           -> ERROR
  fn main(), do: dbg([Enum.reverse([1,2,3]), 9])           -> OK ([[3,2,1], 9])
  fn main(), do: dbg([Enum.reverse([1,2,3]), Enum.reverse([4,5])]) -> ERROR

Error: error[internal/post-resolution-leftover]: quoted function decode failed: invalid any value ref: ExpectedTag { expected: ValueKind(15), found: ValueKind(3) }

Trigger is precise: a list literal whose FINAL element is a call (not a literal). A trailing literal element works; a trailing call element fails. Likely a frontdoor/quote encoding bug where a call in tail position of a list is mis-encoded (no-parens / trailing-do ambiguity at the list close, or the list-element terminator after a call). ValueKind(15) expected vs ValueKind(3) found points at a tag mismatch in quoted_function/quoted_surface decode.

Found incidentally while profiling fz-hyj (amplified-stdlib repro). NOT blocking. Independent of the span/QuotedSourceSpan work.

comments.text:
DONE (folded to 23414196b). Root cause: a quoted AST node is a {head,meta,tail} Struct; split_improper_list/split_improper_pattern_list probed for the improper-list '|' marker via atom_name(&node.head)? UNCONDITIONALLY, but a call's head is itself a nested AST node (Struct), not an atom -> ExpectedTag{Atom(15), found Struct(3)} when a list's LAST element was a call (non-last elements go through decode_expr which already tag-guards). Fix: node_head_is_atom_named() tag-guards (head.tag()==ATOM && atom_name().ok()==Some(name)) before reading head as atom, mirroring decode_expr's guard; applied to both split fns. Symmetric, not a trailing-call shim. Agent swept ~20 sibling atom_name(&node.head)? sites -> all guarded by enclosing dispatch (atom-headed by construction), no other live bugs. Fixture list_literal_trailing_call.fz pins all 5 shapes (single/trailing/leading/middle/all calls); fails-before, passes-after across interp/JIT/AOT. lib 1229/0/9. Self-audited: helper correct, symmetric, no ticket IDs.

NOTE (user decision): the decode-drift CLASS (~20 unenforced head-is-atom invariants in the hand-written reader; shared encode/decode-schema redesign) is deliberately NOT ticketed -- these are caught as unit-test-guarded instances when they surface, not via preemptive redesign.
